original_value: The resolution of contact location is important in many applications in robotics and automation. This is generally done by using an array of contact or tactile receptors, which increases cost and complexity as the required resolution or area is increased. Tactile sensors have also been developed using a continuous deformable medium between the contact and the receptors, which allows few receptors to interpolate the information among them, avoiding the weakness highlighted in the former approach. The latter is generally used to measure contact force intensity or magnitude but rarely used to identify the contact locations. This paper presents a systematic design and characterisation procedure for magnetic-based soft tactile sensors (utilizing the latter approach with the deformable contact medium) with the goal of locating the contact force location. This systematic procedure provides conditions under which design parameters can be selected, supported by a selected machine learning algorithm, to achieve the desired performance of the tactile sensor in identifying the contact location. An illustrative example, which combines a particular sensor configuration (magnetic hall effect sensor as the receptor, a selected continuous medium and a selected sensing resolution) and a specific data-driven algorithm, is used to illustrate the proposed design procedure. The results of the illustrative example design demonstrates the efficacy of the proposed design procedure and the proposed sensing strategy in identifying a contact location. The resulting sensor is also tested on a robotic hand (Allegro Hand, SimLab Co) to demonstrate its application in real-world scenarios.

result.paraphrase: Accurate contact-location resolution is crucial in many robotics and automation tasks. It is typically achieved with arrays of contact or tactile receptors, but higher resolution or larger sensing areas increase cost and complexity. Another approach uses a continuous deformable layer between the contact and the receptors, enabling a small number of receptors to interpolate the contact information and avoid the limitations of the former method. This second approach is usually employed to measure contact force intensity or magnitude, and is rarely used for locating contact points. This paper proposes a systematic design and characterization process for magnetic-based soft tactile sensors that use the deformable-medium approach to determine contact force location. The procedure defines how design parameters can be chosen, together with a selected machine learning algorithm, to meet the desired sensor performance in contact-location identification. An illustrative example combines a specific sensor configuration, comprising a magnetic Hall-effect receptor, a chosen continuous medium, and a selected sensing resolution, with a particular data-driven algorithm to demonstrate the proposed design method. The example results show the effectiveness of the proposed procedure and sensing strategy for identifying contact location. The resulting sensor is also evaluated on an Allegro Hand robotic hand from SimLab Co to show its use in real-world applications.
